summary: This program defines a RobotPet class that can decide whether a pet has enough battery for a walk of a given length, then checks that decision with two assert statements. If both checks hold, the program prints a success message; if either fails, Python stops and shows the message you supplied.

lines.text: This begins the blueprint for a robot pet, so every pet created from it shares the same attributes and behaviour.
The __init__ method runs automatically whenever a new pet is created, and it receives the values that make each pet different.
Storing the battery level on the object is what later lets can_walk compare available energy against the energy a walk demands.
This method answers a single yes-or-no question about the pet, which is exactly the kind of small, predictable behaviour that is easy to test.

lines.code: """Check if the pet has enough energy for a walk of given duration (in minutes)."""
lines.text: A docstring records what the method promises, including the unit of the duration, so a reader never has to guess whether it means minutes or hours.
The rule of the program is that every minute of walking costs two units of battery; naming the result makes the next line read clearly.
The comparison itself evaluates to True or False, so the method hands that value straight back to the caller.
Rover starts with 85 battery, which is deliberately more than the 60 a thirty-minute walk costs.
Beep starts with only 45 battery, giving us a pet that should fail the same walk and so exercises the other branch of the comparison.

lines.code: assert rover.can_walk(30) == True, "Rover should be able to walk for 30 minutes"
lines.text: An assert says "this must be true"; if the expression is false, Python raises an AssertionError and shows the text after the comma.

lines.code: assert beep.can_walk(30) == False, "Beep should not be able to walk for 30 minutes"
lines.text: Testing the negative case matters just as much, because a method that always returned True would pass the first test alone.
This line is only reached when every assert above has held, so seeing it printed is your confirmation that the tests succeeded.
